notes: MCP-stub-backed batch for sift-email (see evals/lib/mcp-stub: gmail_stub.py, docs_stub.py, contacts_stub.py). The executor is a real, separate `claude -p --strict-mcp-config` subprocess run by evals/lib/run-mcp-trials.sh, one turn per eval with no follow-ups: sift runs unattended, so every eval checks that it finishes the run without waiting on the user. The skill sets disable-model-invocation, so every prompt starts with /sift-email, followed by the rubric and log links (eval 1 gives none, for the first run; eval 14 gives links but no Claude Docs server). Fixtures are anchored to 2026-10-10 with the Gmail stub's stub_now at 15:00 UTC, and Important is Gmail's IMPORTANT system label, a needed reply is STARRED, and a tab is one CATEGORY_* label (CATEGORY_PERSONAL or none for Primary), filed by the rubric's Tabs section; the AI label ids are fixed: Label_22 AI/Low priority, Label_23 AI/Junk, Label_27 AI/Bulk, Label_28 AI/Newsletter; Label_1-4 are the user's own (Soccer, Receipts, Newsletter, School). Grade against each trial's eval.json and the gmail, docs, and contacts state-out files and call logs, not the reply's own account. Sift asks no questions and reads no comments: eval 10 checks that an old answered 'Sift:' comment is neither applied nor answered, and eval 32 that a close call the rubric leaves open becomes a dated '(inferred)' rubric line. Evals 28 to 31 cover the rubric as one sift-maintained document: an older rubric brought up to date, evidence rewriting a user's rule, a new Gmail tab added to the Tabs table, and the rubric overriding any skill default. Evals 6, 7, 11, 13, and 14 are the cases where sift must hold back (nothing in the daily review is a signal, the user's own edits, nothing to do, an unauthorized action, a missing connector), and 25 is a learned newsletter that overrides the user's own Not valued line. Log run headings carry their start in epoch seconds as {{epoch:...}} tokens, which fixture-dates.py moves with the dates.
